Every point adds at least one fact ID not used by earlier points; shared context refs are allowed alongside a new fact. Summary may reuse point references. Merge one topic's principle, reason, condition and important example into one compact point; do not make a final leftover catalog. Cover all core fact IDs somewhere in summary or points collectively. Write a concise summary paragraph that synthesizes the central message rather than copying or restating most source sentences. Short sources need a shorter paragraph and fewer points. Use one point per substantive theme where possible, combining its preparation, reasons and essential conditions. Put necessary outline context in the summary instead of making a standalone point for an announced topic count. Do not fragment a theme merely to fill seven slots. Before writing, consolidate all parts into at most 7 global themes. A slot is a theme, never a single-fact inventory or a chapter-by-chapter list. Combine related principles, conditions and examples; each slot may reference several fact IDs. Do not create one point per fact or per source part. Preserve core meanings and closing consequences. Write a short synthesis, not a detailed course catalog, in summary.
